taxonomyNote: Animal Diversity Web treats it as a domesticated form of the African collared dove (S. roseogrisea); NatureServe lists S. roseogrisea, not S. risoria.
fieldMarks: Black semi-collar on the hind neck
Slightly larger than the African collared dove with a shorter tail
behavior: Advertising call is 'koo, krroo'; also a high-pitched excitement call
Displays with bowing and wing-clapping display flights
Eats grains and seeds without husking
habitat: Domestic aviary birds; wild ancestor lives in African scrub, savanna and woodland.

Escaped birds live near people: Animal Diversity Web lists suburban habitat for the ringed turtle-dove, and EDDMapS says African collared doves in the United States, which escaped captivity, inhabit areas near people and are thought unable to survive without food people provide.
range: Sporadic introduced colonies near Los Angeles, in southern Florida and in Illinois.

lookalikes.name: Eurasian collared-dove
lookalikes.howToTell: Animal Diversity Web notes it resembles this species but the ringed turtle-dove is markedly tamer.
